gaps.title: Rejection reason capture not covered by the mockup
gaps.description: DEC-002 confirms a reason is required when rejecting a claim, but the Reject button on the Expense approvals screen has no target and no reason field, dialog or step is shown in the capture. Where the reason is entered, whether it has length or content rules, what happens when it is left empty, and where the reason is later visible (audit log, employee) are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: The customer made the reason mandatory, yet the only observed Reject control is a one-click row button; without a defined capture point the rule cannot be enforced or tested, and the audit log columns shown (When, Who, Action) have no place for the reason.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Claims could be rejected without a reason, breaking a confirmed customer rule, and the audit record of rejections would be incomplete.
research_questions: What are established patterns for capturing a mandatory reason on a reject action in approval workflows, including validation and error messaging?
Which WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria apply to a required free-text field shown in a dialog or inline step (labels, error identification, focus management)?

gaps.title: Audit log entry contents, retention and integrity undefined
gaps.description: REQ-002 (must) requires every approval and rejection to be recorded, but what each entry must contain is not defined (CQ-003 was not answered). The captured log shows only When, Who and Action (for example 'Approved EXP-71'); whether entries must also hold the claim amount, employee, rejection reason, or prior state is unknown, as are how long entries are kept, and whether entries can be edited or deleted by anyone.
gaps.why_it_matters: The audit log is the only must-priority requirement and the subject of the finance export; expense approvals involve money paid to employees, so the log may be relied on for financial audit and disputes.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The log may omit data an auditor needs, be kept for too short a time, or be alterable, which would undermine its purpose as evidence.
research_questions: What fields do established audit-trail practices (for example OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, ISO 27001 A.8.15) recommend for recording approval decisions?
What record-retention periods apply to UK expense and payroll-related records (for example HMRC record-keeping rules)?
What practices are used to make application audit logs append-only or tamper-evident?

gaps.title: Outcome of Approve and Reject not defined
gaps.description: Approve and Reject have no target in the capture, and no claim status column is shown. What the manager sees after acting (row removed, status shown, confirmation message), what happens if the action fails, and whether the audit entry is written in the same operation as the decision so that a decision cannot exist without its log entry are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Approve and Reject are the core actions of this feature, and REQ-002 says every one must be logged; if a decision can succeed while its log write fails, the must-have requirement is broken silently.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Managers cannot tell whether their decision took effect, and decisions may go unrecorded in the audit log.
research_questions: What are common practices for guaranteeing that a business state change and its audit record are stored together or not at all?
How should success and failure of a row-level action be announced to assistive technology under WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages?

gaps.title: Enforcement of the direct-reports-only rule
gaps.description: DEC-001 limits managers to claims from their own direct reports. The capture shows a single claims list with no indication of how it is scoped. Not defined: whether a manager can approve their own claim, who approves a manager's or a top-level employee's claims, what happens when a manager is absent or a reporting line changes while claims are pending, and whether there is any delegation or override.
gaps.why_it_matters: The rule decides who can release money for whom; edge cases such as self-approval and claims with no eligible approver are where expense fraud and stuck claims typically arise.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Claims may be approved by an ineligible person or never be approvable, and reporting-line changes could leave pending claims orphaned.

gaps.title: Reversal or correction of a decision
gaps.description: CQ-002 asked whether a decision can be changed or reversed; DEC-002 answered only the rejection-reason part. Whether an approval or rejection can be undone, by whom, within what window, and how a reversal is reflected in the audit log is not defined. No confirmation step is shown before Approve or Reject.
gaps.why_it_matters: Approve and Reject sit side by side on each row as one-click buttons, so a mis-click is plausible; an approval may lead to payment, so a wrong decision may have financial effect.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Mistaken decisions may be impossible to correct, or corrections may happen outside the system and leave the audit log inaccurate.

gaps.title: Who may view the audit log, and whether roles other than finance may export
gaps.description: REQ-003 grants export to finance staff, and the Audit log is linked from the managers' Expense approvals screen, but who may view the log is not defined (CQ-003 unanswered), nor whether managers see all entries or only their own team's, nor whether roles other than finance may export (DEC-003 did not address this). The Export CSV button is shown without any visible role restriction.
gaps.why_it_matters: The log reveals employee names, claim amounts and decisions across the organisation; reaching it from the managers' screen suggests managers may see other teams' expense data.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Personal and financial data may be visible to or exportable by people who should not have it.

gaps.title: Export scope, columns and failure behaviour
gaps.description: DEC-003 sets the format to a CSV of audit log entries. Still undefined: whether the export covers the whole log or a date range or filter, which columns and encoding are used, how a very large log is handled, what the user sees if export fails, and whether performing an export is itself recorded.
gaps.why_it_matters: Finance staff will use the export as their working copy of approval history; the log grows with every decision, so an unbounded whole-log export will get larger over time.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The export cannot be specified or tested, may time out on large logs, and may not show who took audit data out of the system.
research_questions: What CSV conventions (RFC 4180, UTF-8 with or without BOM) open correctly in common spreadsheet tools used by finance teams?
What practices exist for exporting large datasets from web applications (streaming, background generation) and reporting failures to the user?

gaps.title: Spreadsheet formula injection through exported CSV
gaps.description: The CSV export will contain text entered by users, such as claim descriptions and, per DEC-002, free-text rejection reasons. How such values are treated when they begin with characters a spreadsheet interprets as formulas is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Employees author claim descriptions and finance staff open the exported CSV in spreadsheet tools, so an employee-controlled value could execute in a finance user's spreadsheet.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Exported audit data could be used to attack finance staff machines or alter displayed figures.
research_questions: What does OWASP recommend for preventing CSV/formula injection in exported files, and what are the trade-offs for data fidelity?

gaps.title: Duplicate and concurrent decisions on the same claim
gaps.description: Not defined: what happens if Approve or Reject is clicked twice, if a request is retried after a timeout, or if the claim was already decided (for example in another tab or by another eligible approver) while the list was open. Whether each case produces one or several audit entries is also undefined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Each decision must be logged, so duplicate or conflicting submissions directly corrupt the audit trail, and a claim could end up both approved and rejected.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Duplicate or contradictory audit entries and an uncertain final claim status.
research_questions: What are established techniques for making state-changing approval requests idempotent and detecting stale views (for example idempotency keys, optimistic concurrency with version checks)?

gaps.title: Accessible names and feedback for row actions
gaps.description: The claims table has an unlabelled actions column and each row repeats identical Approve and Reject buttons. How each button identifies the claim it acts on to assistive technology, and how keyboard focus and status are handled after a row changes, are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: With several claims listed, a screen reader user hearing only 'Approve' could approve the wrong employee's claim, which is a financial decision.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Approvals may be misapplied by assistive-technology users and the feature may fail WCAG 2.2 AA.
research_questions: Which WCAG 2.2 criteria (for example 1.3.1, 2.4.6, 4.1.2) govern repeated action buttons in data table rows, and what techniques give them unique accessible names?
How should focus be managed when a table row is removed or updated after an action?

gaps.title: Empty, loading and error states for both screens
gaps.description: Only a default state with one row is shown in the capture for the Expense approvals list and the Audit log. States with no pending claims, no log entries, while loading, and on load failure are not shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: Managers with no direct reports, or none with pending claims, will routinely see an empty approvals list, and a failed load must not look like 'nothing to approve'.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Managers may wrongly conclude there is nothing pending, delaying employee reimbursement.

gaps.title: Volume handling in claims list and audit log
gaps.description: Whether the claims list and audit log support sorting, filtering or paging, their default order, and how many records they are expected to hold are not defined; one row each is shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: The audit log grows with every decision and is never cleared unless a retention rule says so, so it will become long; finance staff may need to find specific claims or periods.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The log may become slow or unusable to browse, and its relationship to export scope stays unclear.

gaps.title: Notification of the employee and downstream effects
gaps.description: Whether the employee is told of an approval or rejection (and of the rejection reason), through which channel, and whether approval triggers payment or another downstream process, is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: A mandatory rejection reason is only useful to the employee if it reaches them; and if approval triggers payment, reversal (GAP-005) becomes harder.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Employees may not learn the outcome of their claims, and integration scope stays unknown.

gaps.title: Time zone and date format of audit timestamps
gaps.description: The audit log shows 'When' as '2 Mar 10:14' with no year or time zone. Which time zone timestamps are recorded and shown in, and how they appear in the CSV export, are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Audit timestamps are evidence; without year and time zone, entries across years or daylight-saving changes are ambiguous, especially once exported.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Exported audit data may be misread or fail to sort correctly in spreadsheets.
research_questions: What timestamp format (for example ISO 8601 with offset or UTC) is recommended for audit logs and machine-readable CSV exports?

gaps.title: Navigation back from the Audit log
gaps.description: A flow from Expense approvals to Audit log is captured, but no link back from the Audit log screen is shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Managers reaching the log from the approvals screen need to return to pending claims; the wider app navigation may exist but was not captured.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Navigation between the two screens cannot be specified.

assumptions.text: DEC-002 answers only the rejection-reason part of CQ-002; whether decisions can be reversed remains open.
assumptions.why: The verbatim answer mentions only the reason requirement.
assumptions.impact: GAP-005 is raised rather than treated as answered.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm with the customer whether decisions can be reversed.

assumptions.text: The Audit log link on the Expense approvals screen does not by itself establish that managers may view the audit log.
assumptions.why: Mockup placement is an observation, not a confirmed permission; REQ-003 names only finance staff for export.
assumptions.impact: View permission is raised as an open question in GAP-006.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm which roles may view the audit log and what scope they see.

assumptions.text: DEC-003 fixes the export format as CSV but does not settle export scope or which other roles may export.
assumptions.why: The verbatim answer addresses only the file type and content type.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm export scope and roles with the customer.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Audit entry contents, retention and viewing permissions are not stated; CQ-003 has no recorded decision.
